sections.title: Basic Concept of Pipes and Cisterns
sections.content: Questions on Pipes and Cisterns are based on the rate at which a tank is filled or emptied. Step 1: Find the rate of each pipe (how much part of the tank it fills or empties in one minute or hour). Step 2: Treat filling pipes as positive work and emptying pipes as negative work. Step 3: Add all the rates to find the net rate. Step 4: Total time = 1 / Net rate.

sections.title: Two Pipes Filling and One Pipe Emptying
sections.content: Step 1: Rate of each filling pipe = 1 / time taken. Step 2: Rate of emptying pipe = 1 / time taken (consider negative). Step 3: Net rate = pipe1 + pipe2 - leak pipe. Step 4: Total time = 1 / net rate. Example: Pipe A fills the tank in 6 hours, Pipe B fills it in 8 hours, and a leak empties it in 12 hours. Net rate = 1/6 + 1/8 - 1/12.

sections.title: Finding Total Capacity of the Tank
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the filling pipe rate in liters per minute. Step 2: Multiply the rate by time to find total filled quantity. Step 3: Subtract the emptying pipe rate if present. Step 4: From the remaining quantity determine the tank's total capacity. Example: If a pipe fills 20 liters per minute and the tank fills in 10 minutes, then capacity = 200 liters.

sections.title: Filled or Emptied Portion of the Tank
sections.content: Step 1: Write the pipe rate in fractional form. Step 2: Multiply by the given time to find the filled part. Step 3: Subtract leakage if present. Step 4: Get the final fraction. Example: If a pipe fills 1/5 of the tank per hour, then in 2 hours it fills 2/5 of the tank.

sections.title: Net Work Concept
sections.content: Step 1: Write the rates of all pipes in the same unit. Step 2: Add the filling rates. Step 3: Subtract the emptying rates. Step 4: Use the net rate to find total time. Example: If net rate = 1/4 tank per hour, the tank will be filled in 4 hours.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not treating emptying pipes as negative rates. 2. Not converting different time units into a common unit. 3. Errors in addition or subtraction while calculating net rate. 4. Forgetting to simplify fractions.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: The most important concept in Pipes and Cisterns is the rate concept. Write each pipe’s work in fraction form, add filling rates and subtract emptying rates. The net rate determines the total time or capacity.

tricks.title: Rate Formula Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Rate of a pipe = 1 / time taken.
tricks.example: If a pipe fills a tank in 5 hours, then rate = 1/5 tank per hour.

tricks.title: Net Work Rule
tricks.explanation: Net rate = sum of all filling pipe rates - emptying pipe rates.

tricks.title: LCM Method
tricks.explanation: Assume total tank capacity as the LCM of given times to solve quickly.

tricks.title: Leakage Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: A leak pipe always performs negative work.
tricks.example: If a leak empties the tank in 12 hours, rate = -1/12.

tricks.title: Fraction Fill Trick
tricks.explanation: Rate × Time = filled portion of the tank.

tricks.title: Capacity Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If rate is given in liters per minute then Capacity = rate × total time.

tricks.title: Unit Conversion Trick
tricks.explanation: Convert all pipe rates into the same unit (minutes or hours).

tricks.title: Quick Net Time Trick
tricks.explanation: Taking the reciprocal of net rate gives total time.
